memories.summary: Sophia started the year in Boston, working late nights in her university lab to finalize the prototype of an autonomous delivery robot. She tested its motion tracking system across hallways, noting improvements in navigation precision.

memories.summary: In Palo Alto, Sophia joined a small robotics startup as a consultant, helping the team debug a malfunctioning vision module. She suggested implementing a depth-aware convolutional model to improve object detection accuracy.
memories.what: Assisting a robotics startup with computer vision optimization.

memories.what: Presenting research and networking at an international robotics conference.

memories.what: Developing and testing drone swarm coordination algorithms.

memories.summary: Sophia spent May in Singapore mentoring high school students in a robotics competition. She guided them in designing obstacle-avoiding bots and gave a motivational talk about women in STEM.
memories.what: Mentoring students and promoting STEM education.

memories.summary: Returning to Tokyo, Sophia collaborated with engineers from a tech company to integrate AI-powered sensors into humanoid robots. She spent a week debugging servo-motor latency and refining gesture control algorithms.
memories.what: Collaborating on humanoid robot sensor integration.

memories.summary: In San Francisco, Sophia demonstrated her delivery robot prototype at a tech expo. The robot successfully recognized dynamic obstacles and rerouted itself through a crowded corridor, earning applause from the audience.
memories.what: Public demo of her autonomous robot at a tech expo.

memories.summary: During a short visit to Berlin, Sophia met her Zurich collaborators again to plan a joint EU-funded robotics proposal. They discussed drone deployment ethics and AI governance in research applications.
memories.what: Writing a research proposal on ethical drone systems.

memories.summary: In Toronto, Sophia gave a guest lecture at a university on the topic of robot-human interaction. She emphasized the importance of empathy-driven design and real-world safety testing in commercial robotics.
memories.what: Delivering a lecture on responsible robotics design.

memories.summary: Sophia concluded her year in Boston by publishing a comprehensive paper summarizing her findings on multi-agent learning for cooperative robotics. She celebrated the milestone with her research team at a local café.
memories.what: Publishing her major research paper on cooperative robotics.
